test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is the CORRECT objective of ISRO's Gaganyaan mission scheduled for launch in 2025?

options.text: Sending Indian astronauts into low-Earth orbit
Sending an unmanned rover to the Moon
Launching a solar probe to study the Sun

solution:
The correct answer is __**Sending Indian astronauts into low-Earth orbit**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Gaganyaan mission** is India's first human spaceflight program, designed to demonstrate the capability to send humans into a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.

• The mission aims to launch a crew of **three members** to an altitude of approximately **400 km** for a duration of **three days** before bringing them safely back to Earth.

• ISRO will utilize the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**, formerly known as **GSLV Mk III**, which has been upgraded to meet **human-rating** standards for safety and reliability.

• The mission consists of an **Orbital Module** which includes a **Crew Module (CM)** for the astronauts and a **Service Module (SM)** containing propulsion and power systems.

• The return journey involves a planned landing in the **Indian Ocean**, where the crew will be recovered by the **Indian Navy** and other agencies.

 **Additional Information__**

• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**:

• Headquartered in **Bengaluru**, it was established on **August 15, 1969**, to harness space technology for national development.

• If successful, India will become the **fourth country** to launch a manned mission, following the **Soviet Union/Russia**, the **USA**, and **China**.

• **Other Mission Objectives**:

• **Bharatiya Antariksh Station**: India plans to establish its own **permanent space station** by **2035**, building on the experience gained from Gaganyaan.

• **Lunar Exploration**: The **Chandrayaan-3** mission successfully landed a rover on the **Moon** in **2023**, with future goals including an Indian landing on the Moon by **2040**.

• **Solar Observation**: The **Aditya-L1** mission was launched in **September 2023** to study the **Sun** from the **Lagrangian Point 1**, marking India's first dedicated solar observatory.
